findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the cleanup callback
findings.body: After a caller invokes the returned disposer, later `"message"` events still invoke `handler`. Repeated attach/dispose cycles also retain stale listeners and increase per-message work. The changed callback is a no-op, while the removed implementation correctly paired `socket.on` with `socket.off`.

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup callback
findings.body:
Any caller invoking the returned disposer expects the registered `"message"` handler to be detached. The no-op leaves it active, causing callbacks after disposal and duplicate listeners when components reconnect or remount.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body:
On a long-lived or reused socket, invoking the disposer no longer ends the handler’s trust lifetime. Subsequent peer-controlled messages still reach handlers associated with terminated sessions or revoked privileges, potentially causing stale-authority actions or cross-session processing; repeated attach/dispose cycles also accumulate active handlers.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
